title: Datasette 1.0a39 and 0.65.4 security releases
raw_text: Datasette 1.0a39 and 0.65.4 security releases Today we're releasing two new security patch versions of Datasette: 1.0a39 and 0.65.4 - one for the current alpha series and one for the stable 0.65.x family. These are security fixes which you should apply if you are running a Datasette instance on the public web - in particular if that instance mixes both public and private tables. Following issues reported by Sevban Dönmez , Alex Garcia and I ran an extensive audit of Datasette using Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-5.6, and GPT-6 Astra. We then spent almost a week collaborating on and reviewing the fixes. They helped find some very subtle bugs. We'll be incorporating security audits by frontier models into all of our development work going forward. Alex came up with a way of splitting the work which I found extremely productive: Alex Garcia and I worked together running and then responding to the audit, working in a shared private repository. For most of the issues we split the work: one of us would create the automated tests highlighting the issue, then the other would implement the fix. This ensured that two separate humans had eyes on each of the issues, in addition to our coding agents running different models. title: Any Nix package, live in your browser
raw_text: Any Nix package, live in your browser Farid Zakaria calls this his " magnum opus of Nix work", and I can see why. trynix.dev provides a qemu-wasm powered x86_64 Linux virtual machine running entirely in your browser through WebAssembly. That VM can then be booted with any Nix package from the past 13 years. They are URL addressable, so you can navigate to this page: https://trynix.dev/?pkg=python3%403.6.2 Then click "Load" and get an interactive shell against a virtual machine running Python 3.6.2 from 2017. Farid is building all sorts of neat things on top of this. One recent example: Review a pull request by booting it introduces trynix-preview , described like this: GitHub action that comments a link on a pull request which lets you boot the PR’s build in the browser using https://trynix.dev . No servers, just browsers. Via Lobste.rs Tags: code-review , linux , webassembly , github-actions

title: Evolving Trends: A Bibliometric Analysis of Academic Librarians’ Publications at Twelve AAU Member Universities (New C&RL Journal Article)
raw_text: The article linked below was recently published by College & Research Libraries (C&RL) Title Evolving Trends : A Bibliometric Analysis of Academic Librarians’ Publications at Twelve AAU Member Universities Authors Pete E. Pascuzzi Purdue University Libraries Jason B. Reed Purdue University Libraries Greenley Goedde Creech Purdue University Libraries Source College & Research Libraries Vol 87, No 5 (2026) Vol 87, No 5 (2026) Abstract The goal of this bibliometric study was to explore the broader publication patterns of academic librarians in both information and library science (ISLS) and interdisciplinary research for the years 2009 to 2023. Web of Science data were collected for 12 academic libraries. The results showed that while the number of ISLS publications has dropped, interdisciplinary publications have increased dramatically with a broad range of disciplines represented, and that collaborations in the medical sciences were a major contributor to this increase. The study suggests that some academic libraries have shifted their priorities over the past 15 years and that the assessment of libraries’ scholarly publications must evolve to capture this shift. title: Native is now the future of mobile at Shopify
raw_text: Native is now the future of mobile at Shopify Shopify are moving from React Native back to separate Swift and Kotlin codebases for their native apps, for the exact reason you would expect: We decided to switch from native to React Native in 2020 for three reasons: Stop building the same features twice Allow developers to work across the stack Spend less time chasing feature parity and more time shipping value [...] Native still means building and maintaining software on two platforms, that cost has not disappeared. What changed is that agents can now do enough of the implementation, translation, testing, and review work that it’s no longer the deciding factor it was in 2020. It's a well-written post, which gives full credit to React Native as a great platform for the six years they were using it. Shopify are the maintainers of three significant React Native libraries: react-native-skia , flash-list , and restyle . The first two are finding new homes; the third "has a smaller user base than our other libraries" and will be archived at the end of 2026. title: Powering AI is an architecture problem
raw_text: On July 22, 2026, a transmission line fault in Ashburn, Virginia—the heart of the world’s largest data center cluster—knocked more than 3 gigawatts of load off the grid in seconds. And it wasn’t the first time. Two years earlier, a single failed surge arrester dropped roughly 60 Virginia facilities and 1,500 megawatts at once. No one could anticipate so much uniform load responding to grid faults the same way, at the same time. The AI power debate is mostly about generation: more turbines, more solar, more transmission. The grid needs more electrons. But the outages in Virginia weren’t supply failures; they were architecture failures. And a giant wave of interconnections is arriving on that same architecture, putting grid reliability at risk. It’s a problem nobody wants to own. Asking more from the grid The grid was built around predictable loads: steel mills, refineries, and houses at dinnertime. Different load sizes, same process—drawing power smoothly, misbehaving occasionally, and recovering gracefully. But AI data centers don’t behave that way. An AI campus can swing 70% of its load in milliseconds during a training run, then trip offline just as fast at the first sign of trouble upstream to protect billions in compute. Each is rational alone. Together, at gigawatt scale, they’re a problem the grid has never solved—and the next wave of data center campuses is planned at exactly that scale. title: This road map could help us decide whether to deploy solar geoengineering
raw_text: A San Francisco nonprofit has published a detailed road map of the experiments, studies, and infrastructure that it says would be needed to make informed decisions about the use of solar geoengineering, MIT Technology Review can reveal. Scientists have now spent half a century exploring the possibility that we could counteract climate change by releasing reflective particles into the stratosphere, mimicking the cooling effects of volcanic eruptions. But even after at least hundreds of studies on the concept, known as stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI), big gaps remain in the scientific understanding of how well it would work and what else it might do—and there has been no systematic plan for clearing up that uncertainty. Reflective, a research organization that funds studies on solar geoengineering, has today attempted to fill that gap with the release of its SAI Research Roadmap . “Our mission is to equip the world with the data and tools required for informed decision-making about sunlight reflection fast enough to matter,” says Dakota Gruener, the organization’s cofounder and chief executive. “Our sense is the world may need to make very consequential decisions on timelines far shorter than our research system is prepared for.” The hope is the exercise will guide scientific efforts and encourage philanthropies or government agencies to fund high-priority work and “responsibly accelerate research,” says Gruener. title: Disclosing AI Use in Academic Research, a New Global Study From Oxford University Press
raw_text: Published today by Oxford University Press (OUP): We have updated our author and editor guidelines on the responsible, appropriate, and transparent use of AI, including a policy outlining what AI use should be disclosed when preparing manuscripts for our journals. In a recent global survey of more than 2,600 researchers, nearly three-quarters (74%) of respondents revealed they were unclear what AI use they should disclose, despite there being strong support for disclosure. With 44% of researchers concerned that disclosing their use of AI will negatively impact how others view their work, and only 36% recording their AI use during their research, our survey emphasizes the growing gap between AI use and disclosure in academic research, and recognizes the need for clear disclosure policies. Direct to Full Text Report (59 pages; PDF) Selected Findings From the Survey: 64% of researchers report AI as beneficial to their research, with over two-thirds (68%) using AI chatbots on the open web for their research, and just under half (49%) using machine translation. AI tools are most commonly used for discovering existing research (55%), summarizing existing research (46%), and editing the write-up of research (45%). Many (68%) agree that AI tools can reduce accessibility barriers, too. However, 35% of those in the arts and humanities never use AI tools in their research, as opposed to 15% and 18% for STM and the social sciences, respectively. title: Can the US battery market untangle from China?
raw_text: The US is hitting records for the rapid growth of its energy storage market. That’ll go a long way to shoring up the grid, increasing reliability and also cutting emissions, since batteries can help store energy from intermittent renewables like wind and solar. Crucially, this is all happening with the help of cheap Chinese batteries, though there’s been a concerted effort to reduce the US’s reliance on them. Most recently, in an executive order in late August, the Trump administration declared a national emergency that essentially bans Chinese batteries from being used in grid-scale energy storage systems. There’s an argument to be made about reducing reliance on any single source of a crucial energy technology. But all this tension raises a broader question for me: How much should countries take advantage of cheap, available tech, versus cutting off major sources to force development of their own factories even if that comes at a higher cost? This is hardly America’s first push to move away from Chinese influence in the battery supply chain. One of the major policy tools used in recent years is restricting the tax credits designed to incentivize use of the new technologies. Limiting the types of projects that are eligible can help reduce the cost of local technologies so they’re more competitive with otherwise cheaper imported options. title: Healthcare AI’s next test is integration
raw_text: The entrance of major AI companies into healthcare is a meaningful and welcome development, accelerating the technical foundation available to the industry. Their models are increasingly capable of processing long clinical records, interpreting complex terminology, comparing documentation against evidence and generating coherent summaries from large volumes of information. For clinicians, operators, and administrative teams who spend significant time searching through fragmented data, these advances are helping reduce cognitive burden and make high-value information easier to access. But healthcare leaders should not confuse model capability with operational capability. Healthcare’s administrative challenges are caused by fragmented information, fragmented workflows, and fragmented accountability, not a lack of information. The industry has spent decades investing in systems that capture activity: electronic health records, billing platforms, payer portals, scheduling systems, call center platforms, and analytics applications. Each system records something important. But few were designed to reason across the full chain of decisions that determines whether patients get timely access, clinicians have the right documentation and providers are reimbursed appropriately. This is the problem that AI must now confront. title: Vacature: Metadataspecialist digitale preservering bij de KB nationale bibliotheek
raw_text: Als metadataspecialist digitale preservering werk je aan de toekomst van de nationale digitale collectie. Jij zorgt dat wat vandaag wordt gearchiveerd, ook over tientallen jaren nog vindbaar en begrijpelijk is. Wat ga je doen? De KB beheert miljoenen digitale objecten, zoals webarchieven, gedigitaliseerde boeken en tijdschriften en born-digital publicaties. Om deze collecties ook op de lange termijn vindbaar en begrijpelijk te houden, is betrouwbare metadata essentieel. Daar draag jij als metadataspecialist direct aan bij. Je werkt met een gespecialiseerd preserveringssysteem waarin metadata wordt vastgelegd over onder andere de herkomst, geschiedenis en technische eigenschappen van bestanden. Je specificeert, implementeert, test en documenteert deze metadata en stelt de specificaties op voor transformaties tussen verschillende (meta)dataformaten. Dit werk wordt ondersteund met specialistische tooling. Daarbij werk je nauw samen met collega’s zoals contentanalisten, informatiespecialisten en digital preservation officers. Ook deel je actief kennis binnen en buiten de KB, bijvoorbeeld via presentaties of deelname aan gebruikersgroepen en congressen. title: Directeur van door Trump tegengewerkte Smithsonian-instituut vertrekt
raw_text: Directeur Lonnie Bunch van het Amerikaanse Smithsonian-instituut stapt na zeven jaar op. Het instituut staat onder druk sinds het aantreden van president Donald Trump. De manier waarop Smithsonian de Amerikaanse geschiedenis en samenleving presenteert staat haaks op het MAGA-gedachtegoed. Trump heeft daarom de aanval geopend op het Smithsonian, dat tientallen nationale musea, bibliotheken en onderwijs- en onderzoeksinstituten omvat. Tentoonstellingen en collecties moeten worden geschrapt en de regering dreigde recent subsidie aan het Smithsonian helemaal stop te zetten. Het instituut bestaat al sinds de 19de eeuw en functioneert onafhankelijk van de regering. Vrijwillig vertrek Tegen The New Yor k Times heeft Bunch, de eerste zwarte Amerikaan aan het hoofd van het Smithsonian, gezegd dat kritiek vanuit het Witte Huis geen aanleiding is geweest voor zijn vertrek. ‘Het was simpelweg gewoon tijd’, aldus Bunch, die nu 73 jaar is. Hij geeft wel aan dat de baan erg stressvol is geweest de laatste jaren. Eerder was Bunch verantwoordelijk voor de opening van het Nationaal Museum voor Afro-Amerikaanse Geschiedenis en Cultuur aan de National Mall in Washington D.C.. Het museum is onderdeel van het Smithsonian en wordt regelmatig onder vuur genomen door de MAGA-beweging. Het museum zou te veel nadruk leggen op het slavernijverleden van de Verenigde Staten. title: Steeds meer jongvolwassenen vinden weg naar de bieb
raw_text: Steeds meer volwassenen zijn lid van de openbare bibliotheek. Vooral onder jongvolwassenen is de groei groot: het aantal bibliotheekleden tussen de 18 en 30 jaar nam met 22 procent toe. Verder kwamen er 35 vestigingen bij, waarmee het hoogste aantal bibliotheekvestigingen sinds 2014 in Nederland is bereikt. In totaal waren ruim 3,8 miljoen Nederlanders lid van de bibliotheek, 3 procent meer dan een jaar eerder. Ook steeg het aantal bezoeken tot bijna 60 miljoen. Dat blijkt uit de jaarlijkse bibliotheekstatistieken (2025) van de KB nationale bibliotheek en het CBS. Staatssecretaris Tielen (Onderwijs en Emancipatie) : “De bibliotheek zit in de lift en dat is goed nieuws! Want de bieb helpt kinderen en volwassenen groeien. Je kunt er leren, nieuwe ideeën opdoen, anderen ontmoeten en natuurlijk boeken lenen en lezen. Zo helpt de bieb – als leeshoek van de wijk – ook het leesplezier én de leesvaardigheid vergroten. Dat is superbelangrijk, want taal heb je nodig voor alles.” Jongvolwassenen vinden de bibliotheek In 2025 steeg het aantal volwassen leden met 5 procent. title: Now Available: Clarivate Releases Pulse of the Library 2026 Survey Report
raw_text: From Clarivate : Clarivate today released the Pulse of the Library 2026 report. Now in its third year, the global survey examines how libraries are responding to technological change, including AI, shifting priorities and growing demands on staff and resources. The findings reveal that Mainland China recorded the highest level of AI implementation, with 28% reporting moderate to active implementation, more than double the rate in 2024 and well above the 16% global figure. The report also shows a widening gap between libraries moving beyond experimentation with AI and those still in the earliest stages of AI adoption. 51% of libraries in active implementation operate under joint library and IT governance, against 26% of the sample overall, signaling the importance of structured governance models and interdepartmental collaboration. Oren Beit-Arie, Senior Vice President, Strategy & Innovation, Academia & Government at Clarivate, said: “For libraries, AI marks a continuous shift along with a set of hard choices about when to adopt, when to hold back and how to protect academic integrity and library core values. What stands out in this year’s research are the differences between libraries choosing to experiment, learn and build confidence with AI and those taking a wait-and-see approach, whether by choice or because resources are limited.” Other key findings from the report include: Concerns are evolving as implementation advances. title: Building Leadership Through Associations: A Conversation with Loida Garcia-Febo
raw_text: How can library associations strengthen leadership and help library and information professionals respond to increasingly complex and uncertain environments? On 25 June 2026, Loida Garcia-Febo, Chair of the IFLA Management of Library Associations Section (MLAS) , joined a conversation with Roxana Huaman Huriarte, Chair of the IFLA Latin America and the Caribbean Regional Division , and Nick Boxem, Chair of the IFLA Europe Regional Division , both members of the IFLA Regional Council leadership group. The conversation explored leadership within IFLA and library associations, and how strategic planning, capacity building and professional networks can help organisations and individuals respond more effectively to change. Leadership is a capacity that can be developed Leadership is not simply linked to holding a formal position but it is a capacity that can be intentionally developed through experience, training, mentoring, coaching and opportunities to work with others. For library associations, this means creating environments where current and emerging leaders can learn, test ideas, build confidence and develop the skills required to guide organisations through change. Garcia-Febo highlighted the importance of leadership training, mentoring and coaching, alongside team building and effective communication. title: Samenwerking bibliotheek Gelderland Zuid (Nijmegen) met eigenaren minibiebs
raw_text: Nijmegen telt honderden minibiebs, de kleine boekenkastjes die je in de straat vindt. Bibliotheek Gelderland Zuid/Bibliotheek Mariënburg (OBGZ) besloot samen te werken met de eigenaren van deze minibiebs, als opstap naar de bibliotheek. Wouter van Balveren, innovatiemanager bij OBGZ (Nijmegen en omstreken) vertelt aan Probiblio.nl dat de bieb de kleine boekenkastjes niet als bedreiging ziet, maar juist als stimulans. ‘De eigenaren zijn enthousiaste mensen die van lezen houden en het leuk vinden om boeken en verhalen met anderen te delen. In die zin zijn het eigenlijk ambassadeurs van leesplezier, net als wij. Daarnaast past het goed bij onze missie: wij staan voor leesplezier, verhalen en toegang tot boeken voor iedereen.’ OBGZ ziet de minibiebs dus als een soort opstap naar de bibliotheek. ‘Wij proberen natuurlijk met onze vestigingen in allerlei wijken zichtbaar te zijn, maar minibiebs zitten echt in de haarvaten van de samenleving. Die staan gewoon in woonwijken, soms bijna in iedere straat.’ De Nijmeegse bibliotheek ondersteunt de minibiebs op verschillende manieren. ‘We kijken naar waar wij als openbare bibliotheek iets kunnen toevoegen. Dat kan collectie zijn, maar ook praktische ondersteuning of ontmoeting.’ De eigenaren hadden volgens Van Balveren behoefte aan drie dingen: collectie, fysieke ondersteuning en inspiratie en ontmoeting. title: Digital Preservation: Internet Archive Releases Online Archive (199,000 Articles) of BET Journalism No Longer Available on the Live Web
raw_text: From the Internet Archive (via Bluesky, X, and Mastodon): Much of BET’s digital journalism is no longer available on the live web. Internet Archive has preserved more than 199,000 BET articles over the years. They can now be accessed through The Wayback Machine & a new pilot explorer: https:// wayback-labs.sf.archive.org/bet-explorer/ Background From Huff Post: Black Entertainment Television, more commonly known as BET, has removed all digital articles from its website in a push to prioritize video content, HuffPost’s Phil Lewis reported Friday. Multimedia reporting remains on the site and BET’s social channels. However, the move to erase the written content came without warning, leaving many writers with no trace of their work, Lewis reported. “Years of news articles are now gone forever,” he wrote. While BET was once known as the pinnacle of Black media, its decision to remove these digital articles adds to an already fragile state of journalism, especially the Black press, as the Trump administration continues to target press freedom and diversity, equity and inclusion. title: New Freckle Project Report Examines 15 Years of Public Library Use
raw_text: From EveryLibrary Institute: A new Freckle Project Report, “15 Years of IMLS Figures” , looks at national public library statistics from 2010 through 2024 and identifies a striking contrast: American public libraries have more facilities, more staff, and higher levels of funding than at any point in the period examined, while several major measures of physical library use remain substantially below their 2010 levels. The Freckle Project is led by researcher Tim Coates, and its publication is supported by the EveryLibrary Institute. The August 2026 Report examines 15 years of data from the Institute of Museum and Library Services on America’s public libraries. In 2024, the United States had 17,580 public library facilities and 147,289 library employees, while public libraries received nearly $18 billion for operations and another $1.6 billion for capital expenditures. Yet annual visits declined from approximately 1.57 billion in 2010 to 869 million in 2024, while total circulation fell from approximately 2.47 billion to 1.71 billion. Coates’s analysis highlights an especially significant decline in adult physical circulation. After subtracting electronic and children’s circulation from total circulation, he estimates that this category fell approximately 68 percent between 2010 and 2024. title: Bibliothecaris VS die zich verzette tegen LHBTQ+-censuur ontvangt schikking na ontslag
raw_text: Saline County in het Amerikaanse Arkansas moet 275.000 dollar betalen in een zaak tegen een bibliotheekdirecteur die zich verzette tegen censuur van LHBTQ+-boeken op de kinderafdeling. Ze werd daarop ontslagen. Een burgerrechtenorganisatie spande een rechtszaak aan en het kwam tot een schikking. Burgerrechtenorganisatie ACLU van Arkansas greep in toen directeur Patty Hector in 2023 was ontslagen vanwege haar kritiek op een verordening die voorschreef dat boeken met ‘seksuele inhoud of afbeeldingen’ uit de kinderafdeling moesten worden verwijderd. ‘Zwijgen nooit de oplossing’ ‘Het opkomen voor de vrijheid om te lezen heeft me mijn baan gekost, en de carrière waar ik zo van hield, maar ik heb nooit geloofd dat zwijgen de oplossing was’, zegt Hector tegen Advocate .com . ‘Bibliotheken zijn van iedereen. Bibliothecarissen moeten hun gemeenschap volgens professionele normen van dienst kunnen zijn, zonder bang te hoeven zijn voor politieke represailles. Ik hoop dat deze schikking een signaal afgeeft aan bibliothecarissen en andere ambtenaren in heel Arkansas dat hun stem en hun grondwettelijke rechten ertoe doen.’ Hectors ontslag viel samen met een Amerikaanse conservatieve campagne om de toegang tot boeken te beperken, waaronder veel titels met LHBTQ+-thema’s. Hector stelde destijds dat deze boeken niet als ongeschikt voor kinderen mogen worden beschouwd. ‘Het is niet illegaal om homo of trans te zijn’, zei ze tijdens een openbare hoorzitting.
